prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck‑accident case — the right lawyer depends on your case facts, severity of injuries, the defendant (independent driver vs. big trucking company), and whether you need a lawyer who will try the case in court or who focuses on negotiated settlements. Instead of one name, here’s a practical way to find the best personal‑injury lawyer in Dallas for your truck accident.

What to look for
- Trucking experience: significant, recent trucking/trailer/CMV cases (not just general car crashes).
- Knowledge of federal & state trucking rules (FMCSA, DOT, driver logs, maintenance records).
- Trial experience and resources: trucking cases often require expert witnesses and costly investigation; make sure the firm can front those costs.
- Record: documented verdicts/settlements, client reviews, peer ratings.
- Communication: clear point of contact, responsiveness, and a written fee agreement.
- Local experience: familiarity with Dallas courts, judges, and local medical providers.
- Contingency fee and expenses policy: understand percentage and how case expenses are handled.

Where to search and verify credentials
- State Bar of Texas and Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral.
- “Super Lawyers,” “Best Lawyers,” and Martindale‑Hubbell (peer ratings).
- Client review sites (Google, Avvo) — look for patterns, not single reviews.
- News articles for big verdicts/settlements.
- Ask for references from past clients or for sample case results in similar cases.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled in the past 3 years?
- Have you handled cases against large trucking companies and obtained trucking company records?
- Do you have trial experience? Will you take this to trial if necessary?
- Who will handle the case day‑to‑day (attorney vs. paralegal)?
- Fee arrangement and who pays investigation costs up front?
- Typical timeline and likely outcomes for a case like mine?
- Can you provide references or examples of similar results?

What to bring to your consultation
- Police report, photos of scene/vehicles/injuries, witness contacts.
- Medical records and bills (even initial ER records).
- Insurance information from all parties.
- Any employer/driving logs or truck company info if you have it.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a dollar amount or guaranteed win.
- Requests for large upfront fees beyond reasonable costs.
- Vague answers about who will handle the case or how expenses are paid.
- Poor communication during initial contact.

Want help narrowing choices?
If you want, tell me a few details (your Dallas zip code, how severe the injuries are, whether the truck was commercial, whether you’ve already been contacted by insurers) and I can suggest how to find and compare 3–5 highly rated Dallas truck‑accident attorneys or give a short list of firms to contact.
